title: Games Specialist (all genders)
description:
At Cardmarket, people come first.

Our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels safe, appreciated, and inspired. A place where you enjoy coming to work and feel good about heading home at the end of the day.

Open communication is at the heart of our culture. Only by talking openly about challenges, big or small, can we find solutions together. Cardmarket connects people across continents, regardless of skin colour, origin, religion, nationality, gender, or sexual orientation. We treat everyone equally and expect the same from all applicants. Our strength lies in our diverse perspectives and the shared commitment to move forward together as an inclusive team.

To strengthen our Games Department, we are looking for a passionate Games Specialist to help us tackle the challenges of our booming TCG catalogue and support the continued growth of our game portfolio. In this role, you will be an integral part of the Games Team, collaborating closely with the Marketing and Customer Support departments, providing valuable TCG expertise to support informed decision-making and effective problem-solving. Your passion for Trading Card Games and deep involvement in the TCG community will be key to helping us deliver game-specific content, insights, and solutions with the consistency and quality our users expect. Together, we will continue to enhance the Cardmarket experience for players, collectors, and enthusiasts across a growing range of games.
  • Managing our TCG product catalogue across multiple Games and categories
  • Assisting Support with the resolution of Game-related enquiries
  • Contributing with Game expertise for Marketing content, campaigns or events
  • Build and maintain documentation regarding workflow processes, ideas and projects
  • Being an active voice in the innovation and improvement of our TCG product catalogue
  • Spreading the enthusiasm and knowledge for TCG's within the company by organizing and hosting internal workshops, gatherings and events
  • Proven extensive knowledge and scope of awareness of the TCG industry and sources of information, with expert level mastery of at least two different Games, including but not limited to a wide coverage perception of the Games' catalogue releases and event schedules; deep understanding of gameplay mechanics; and understanding the nuances, trends and general sentiments of their respective communities
  • A specialization in the Bandai universe of TCG's is preferred
  • History of using and generally understanding the meanders of Cardmarket from a user perspective is deeply recommended
  • Demonstrated remarkable interest for TCG's with a long history of involvement, whether in collecting, community or competitive aspects, as well as ease for adaptability to learn and explore new Games
  • Experience with Microsoft Office Suite is essential; digital task management, presentation, organizational and documentation tools, such as the Atlassian Suite is highly valued
  • Knowledge in basic image editing or graphic asset creation is an advantage
  • Proficiency in the English language
  • Very strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Capacity to work simultaneously in a cooperative teamwork environment as well as being able to perform autonomously
  • Reliability, professionalism, ownership of responsibility and forward critical-thinking
  • Presence in Berlin & valid work permit for Germany is required!
Imagine a workplace where passion, trust, and personal responsibility are part of everyday working life.
A place where people enjoy coming together, sharing ideas, laughing together, while at the same time working with a high level of professionalism.That’s exactly what you’ll find at Cardmarket.

  • Your everyday work
    You will work in a full-time position (39 hours per week) at our office in Berlin, a place where creative energy, exchange, and focus come together. At the same time, we offer a hybrid working model and provide you with all the equipment you need for your work.
    Thanks to flexible working hours with clearly defined core hours, you can structure your day in a way that allows work and private life to harmonize well.

  • Community & Culture
    We meet each other as equals. An informal, first-name culture is a given, from interns to management. We believe that great results are achieved where people feel seen, heard, and valued.
    Our shared passion for trading card games connects us, at work and beyond. It symbolizes what defines us: curiosity, strategy, teamwork, and the drive to continuously challenge ourselves.

  • Vacation & further benefits
    Five weeks of paid vacation as well as a Germany-wide public transport ticket (Deutschlandticket) that supports you flexibly in your everyday life.
    A lunch allowance (up to €7.67 per working day) as well as free drinks and snacks are also part of our benefits.

  • Your development matters
    Standing still is not an option for us, at least not in a positive sense.
    With a personal annual learning budget of €1,500, we deliberately invest in your development: conferences, courses, books, or new skills. You decide what helps you move forward.

  • Mental & physical health
    We know: Great performance can only happen when people are doing well.
    That’s why we support you with an Urban Sports Club membership for your physical balance, our collaboration with DearEmployee, which offers anonymous, professional psychological support, and the Women of Cardmarket & LGBTQIA+ Group, which promotes exchange, visibility, and empowerment.

    In short
    With us, you won’t find anonymous open-plan offices or rigid structures, but a work environment with heart, values, and genuine appreciation, a place where you’re not only allowed to be yourself, but expected to be, take responsibility, and continue developing, professionally and especially personally.

title: Senior UA Creative Strategist - Mobile Games
description:
The Role

We are looking for a sharp, highly curious UA Creative Strategist to help us decide what advertising creatives we should make and why.

This is not primarily a video editing or art production role. Your job is to stay ahead of the mobile games advertising market, spot emerging creative opportunities, understand what is working and what is becoming stale, and turn those insights into strong concepts and clear production briefs.

You will sit at the intersection of creative, user acquisition, games and data.

We want someone who watches the market closely, studies competitors, understands internet culture and short-form video, experiments aggressively, and is constantly asking:

“What should we test next?”

You will work with our UA team and with internal and external creators, editors, artists, AI tools and production partners to turn those ideas into ads.
What You’ll Do

Own Our UA Creative Direction

  • Develop a continuous pipeline of new video ad concepts, hooks, formats and creative hypotheses.
  • Decide which ideas are worth producing and testing based on market trends, player psychology, competitor activity and our own performance data.
  • Build a weekly creative roadmap rather than waiting for production requests.
  • Push beyond obvious variations of existing ads and actively search for new creative angles.

Hunt for Trends and Creative Opportunities

  • Constantly research mobile game advertising across TikTok, Meta, YouTube, AppLovin, Google, Unity, Mintegral and emerging channels.
  • Study successful ads from both direct competitors and completely different genres and industries.
  • Deconstruct winning creatives by looking at the hook, pacing, storytelling structure, gameplay, visual treatment, sound, creator style, emotional trigger and CTA.
  • Track broader TikTok, Reels, Shorts, creator and internet culture trends and identify which ones can be translated into performance advertising.
  • Maintain a living library of interesting ads, formats, hooks and creative patterns.

Turn Insights Into Things We Can Actually Make

  • Write clear, production-ready creative briefs, scripts, storyboards and references.
  • Explain not just what to make, but the hypothesis behind the idea and what we are trying to learn.
  • Give strong creative direction and feedback to video editors, motion designers, game capture teams, UGC creators, AI creators and external agencies.
  • Help producers and artists understand the intent of a concept without prescribing every frame.
  • Review work in progress and push execution until the original creative idea comes through clearly.

Build a Modern Creative Testing Machine

  • Work closely with UA managers to understand CTR, IPM, CVR, CPI, ROAS, retention and other creative performance signals.
  • Identify why a creative worked rather than simply declaring it a winner.
  • Turn winning ads into structured families of new hypotheses rather than endless minor variations.
  • Kill weak directions quickly and double down aggressively when a concept shows promise.
  • Watch for creative fatigue and ensure the pipeline always has genuinely fresh ideas entering testing.

Use AI Aggressively, but Intelligently

  • Stay current with AI image, video, voice, scripting and editing tools.
  • Use AI to prototype ideas, explore concepts and generate variations rapidly.
  • Understand where AI production is good enough, where human production is better, and when the two should be combined.
  • Experiment with AI-native formats and workflows rather than treating AI only as a cheaper production tool.
  • Help us continuously evaluate new creative tools, platforms and production partners.

Direct External Production

  • Identify and brief specialist agencies, UGC creators, freelance editors, AI studios and playable ad providers when appropriate.
  • Evaluate external creative partners based on performance, speed and creative thinking, not simply production polish.
  • Give vendors decisive feedback and keep projects moving.
  • Help us build a flexible production network capable of executing very different kinds of ideas quickly.

Creative Formats You Should Be Comfortable With

You do not need to personally produce all of these, but you should understand how and when to use them:

  • Gameplay-led video
  • TikTok, Reels and Shorts-native ads
  • UGC and creator-style ads
  • Gameplay reviews and reaction formats
  • Narrative and story-driven ads
  • Failure, challenge and transformation formats
  • Humor, memes and culturally relevant concepts
  • AI-generated and AI-assisted video
  • 2D and 3D animation
  • Live action
  • Playable and interactive ads
  • Static and lightweight motion concepts
  • We care much more about choosing the right format for the idea than having a preferred production style

What This Role Is Not

This is not a traditional brand Creative Director role.

It is not primarily a video editor position.

It is also not a UA media buying position.

We are hiring the person who sits between those disciplines. This person is responsible for understanding the market, generating the hypotheses, choosing the creative directions, briefing the people who make them, and learning from the results.

What Success Looks Like

You have created a repeatable rhythm where we always know:

What are we testing? Why are we testing it? What did we learn? What should we make next?

Over time, we should see a larger and more diverse pipeline of strong creative ideas, faster learning cycles, more creative winners, less dependence on a small number of exhausted concepts, and better UA performance as a result.

Above all, we want someone who develops a reputation inside the company for constantly bringing us ideas we would not have thought of ourselves.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • Around 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in mobile games, mobile apps, performance creative, creative strategy, advertising or a closely related field.
  • Strong understanding of mobile game UA creative and performance advertising.
  • Exceptional instinct for short-form video, including hooks, pacing, storytelling, visual communication and attention.
  • Strong analytical thinking and comfort interpreting creative performance data.
  • Ability to look at an advertisement and explain why it works.
  • Ability to turn insights into clear creative hypotheses and actionable briefs.
  • Deep curiosity about games, advertising, internet culture, creators and emerging formats.
  • Strong familiarity with current generative AI creative tools and workflows.
  • Excellent communication and creative feedback skills.
  • High initiative. You should naturally research, experiment and bring us ideas without waiting to be asked.
  • Comfortable challenging existing assumptions when you believe there is a better direction.

Nice to Have

  • Previous mobile game Creative Strategist or Creative Producer experience.
  • Experience with casual or hybrid-casual games.
  • Experience working directly with Meta, TikTok, Google or major mobile ad networks.
  • Familiarity with creative intelligence tools such as Sensor Tower, AppMagic, Apptica, Meta Ads Library or TikTok’s creative tools.
  • Experience briefing and managing UGC creators or external creative agencies.
  • Knowledge of playable ads.
  • Basic hands-on ability with CapCut, Premiere, After Effects or similar tools.
  • Ability to quickly make a rough edit, AI prototype or visual mockup to communicate an idea.
  • Game capture, Unity or other game development familiarity.

Benefits

  • Market competitive, tax-free USD salaries
  • Paid Time Off
  • Performance Bonus
  • Annual Performance Reviews

title: User Experience Design Manager
location: Ho Chi Minh, Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam
description:
User Experience Design Manager

Location: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

Workplace Type: On-site


About the Role

ACB is seeking a visionary User Experience Design Manager to spearhead the future of customer experience within the rapidly evolving financial industry. In a landscape where products, interest rates, and technology are increasingly replicable, customer experience has emerged as the most sustainable competitive advantage. At ACB, we are embarking on a comprehensive transformation journey with the goal of creating simpler, smarter, and more customer-centric experiences across the entire service lifecycle. This is more than just digitalization; it's about redesigning how customers interact with their bank, from everyday transactions and credit needs to future wealth management solutions. As a User Experience Design Manager within the Office of Transformation, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and elevating customer experiences across the bank's digital platforms.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and enhancement of customer experiences across all digital platforms, focusing on strategic transformation initiatives.
  • Drive the digitalization of credit journeys for individual customers, ensuring a seamless and intuitive user experience.
  • Oversee the digitalization of non-credit journeys for individual customers, optimizing touchpoints and interactions.
  • Develop and enhance Wealth Management and Asset Management solutions through strategic partnerships within the ecosystem, focusing on user-centric design.
  • Design and optimize end-to-end customer journeys across various digital channels, ensuring consistency and effectiveness.
  • Conduct in-depth customer behavior research to inform design decisions and identify areas for improvement.
  • Create user flows, wireframes, and prototypes to visualize and test design concepts.
  • Implement data-driven improvements to enhance user experiences based on real-world usage and feedback.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Business, Product Owners, Technology, Data teams, and other stakeholders to ensure successful implementation of designs.
  • Mentor and guide a team of UX designers, fostering a culture of innovation and excellence.


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in User Experience (UX) design for large-scale digital products.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience leading or being primarily responsible for complex transformation programs or product development initiatives.
  • Proven experience working within the banking, finance, insurance, or financial services sectors.
  • Demonstrated ability in customer behavior research, user flow design, wireframing, prototyping, and data-driven experience optimization.
  • Strong experience in cross-functional collaboration with business, product, technology, and data teams.
  • Excellent leadership and team management skills, with the ability to inspire and guide a design team.
  • A strategic mindset, capable of understanding the business, operational, and technological implications of UX design.
  • Proficiency in UX design tools and methodologies.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate design decisions to diverse stakeholders.
  • A passion for creating exceptional customer experiences and driving business impact.


Additional Information

This is a unique opportunity to significantly impact the customer experience for millions of users within one of the bank's major transformation programs. You will tackle real-world challenges in customer experience, digital transformation, retail banking, and wealth management, with the chance to directly influence business growth and customer satisfaction across the entire ACB network. If you believe customer experience is the nexus of strategy, technology, and innovation, and you aspire to leave a lasting mark on the transformation journey of a leading Vietnamese bank, we encourage you to apply or contact us directly to learn more about this exciting opportunity at ACB.

title: Credentialing Specialist
description:

The Credentialing Specialist works as a part of the administrative team and is responsible for ensuring that healthcare professionals and the organization are qualified and meet the necessary requirements to provide services to patients. The individual will verify and organize all aspects of the credentialing and privileging processes and maintain current files on providers, pharmacists, technicians, nurses, medical assistants, and other staff as deemed necessary. Functions include but are not limited to processing credentialing applications, performing primary source verifications, coordinating privileging forms, ensuring documents in credentialing software stay updated and organized, and staying updated on guidelines and applicable state and federal requirements.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  1. Maintains compliance with all regulatory and accrediting institutions.

  4. Works directly with Johnson Health Center (JHC) staff regarding all credentialing and privileging needs and updates and responds to internal and external inquiries in a timely manner.

  1. Maintains credentialing software to track and manage healthcare professional credentials.

Collaborates with Compliance, HR, Billing, and Central Verification Officer (CVO) to facilitate and ensure smooth hand off during the credentialing process, as well as informing them of credentialing issues. Ensures proctoring is completed and signed off on all new providers and other providers as necessary.

  1. Monitors credentialing software to ensure each provider has the appropriate and up-to-date privileges.

Every individual associated with Johnson Health Center will be treated with dignity and respect. Our actions reflect our commitment to honesty, openness, truthfulness, accuracy and ethical behavior. We are accountable for the decisions we make and the outcome of those decisions.

We continually seek out ways to enhance the patient experience and promote an environment of continuous quality improvement.

We are advocates and instruments of positive change, encouraging employees to engage in responsible risk-taking and working to make a difference. Out of the box thinking enables us to build on successes and learn from failures.

We work across functional boundaries for the good of the organization. Our collaborative approach ensures participation, learning and respect and serves to improve the quality of patient care. title: Planning Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The role of the Planning Specialist is to provide quality planning and technical support, as it relates to the Person-Centered Planning (PCP) process and Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS) billing. Additionally, this role provides basic case management oversight as it relates to information contained in ICM and communications with teams.

Essential Functions

  • Support the PCP Process
    • Manage and follow the PCP process for people who receive community living, meaningful day, CDS, employment, supported living, or other support services from The Arc of Howard.
    • Plan high-quality, individually tailored goals and provide resources, outcomes, goals, and completion for the people supported; ensure goals are relevant, measurable, and meet criteria.
    • Collect, coordinate and update information for PCP preparation (previous plan progress, Health Risk Screening Tool (HRST) requests, SIS review, behavior plans, Nursing Plan of Care (NPOC), assessments, etc.), pre-planning using the Detailed Service Authorization Tool (DSAT, Cost Detail etc.), development (SIP) and according to all State and Federal regulations (including interim meetings).
    • Complete pre-planning using tools from Charting the Lifecourse with each person receiving services before prep meetings with the full PCP team.
    • Review the draft and final person-centered plans for accuracy as it relates to the person.
  • Leadership and Training
    • Lead and train agency staff to support person-centered initiatives, plans, outcomes, and goals.
    • Provide guidance on the specific needs of people with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities.
    • Assist with documentation training in ICM as needed.
  • Scheduling
    • Manage PCP scheduling and ensure adequate representation of The Arc staff and coordinating with the Coordinators of Community Services.
  • Process Improvement
    • Recommend new approaches, policies, and procedures to improve the efficiency of departmental services.
  • Funding and Service Development
    • Work with teams and the person supported to explore all waivered services to ensure needs and desires are met.
    • Initiate funding requests with the Coordinators of Community Services for new and modified supports and services.
    • In the absence of the Director, complete the DSAT as requested by the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration.
  • Case Management
    • Maintain regular contact with all members of the team in support of the person.
    • Monitor incidents and ensure team members are notified in a timely manner.
    • Act as an initial point of contact for Coordinators of Community Services.
    • Maintain bi-monthly contact with all persons supported. In-person visits are a priority.
  • Monitoring
    • Monitor and review documentation as it relates to goals and outcomes, nursing services, behavior supports, and overall compliance related documentation at least every 90 days. Work with agency personnel and other team members when follow up is needed or documentation is not present.
    • Monitor and review PCP approvals and Service Authorizations in LTSS to ensure accuracy.
  • Individual Support
    • Ensure individuals are supported in living the life of their choosing through their Person-Centered Plan (PCP).
    • Monitor and facilitate the BSS process with the BSS provider. Attend the Human Rights Committee in support of the BSS. Work with the DSMs and Program Managers to ensure staff are trained on the current BSS plan. Behavioral services.
  • Documentation
    • Ensure accurate and timely completion of program documentation.
    • Maintain and monitor files for those we support for compliance with regulatory agencies.
    • Maintain up-to-date records and documents in the Electronic Health Records, iCare Manager (ICM) and program files including the PCP documents, entry of outcomes and goals, face sheet, behavior support plan, tracking charts and other documents relevant to the person and their services.
  • Health and Safety
    • Monitor and address the health and medical needs of individuals, promptly reporting any concerns.
  • Compliance
    • Work with Quality Enhancement Department regarding OHCQ investigations and Licensing Visits.
  • Benefits
    • Monitor existing benefits and assist the Benefits Coordinator in the submission of documentation for eligibility paperwork (i.e. SSI, SSA, Medicaid Waiver, Medical Assistance, food stamps, HUD).
  • Flexibility
    • Be open to additional tasks and responsibilities as assigned.

Other Functions

  • Promote Person-Centered Philosophy: Champion person-centered planning and self-direction within the agency and through external provider networks.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by Executive Director.

Physical & Mental Demands

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable people with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, employees are regularly required to sit, walk and stand; talk or hear, both in person and by telephone; use hands repetitively to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; reach with hands and arms; and lift up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision and the ability to adjust focus. Ability to drive is a requirement of this position.

Mental Demands

While performing the duties of this job, employees are regularly required to use written and oral communication skills; read and interpret, data information and documents; analyze and solve non-routine and complex problems; use math and mathematical reasoning; observe and interpret situations; learn and apply new information or skills; perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks; work under intensive deadlines with frequent interruptions; and interact with the community stakeholders including elected and appointed officials, staff, people served, the public and others encountered in the course of work.

Work Environment

This position is full-time in a professional office environment and out in the community. The role routinely uses standard office equipment.

Work Schedule

This position is full-time, 40 hours per week. A typical work schedule is Monday through Friday during The Arc office hours from 8:30a-4:30p with some flexibility to accommodate occasional meetings outside regular office hours.

title: Product Manager, Peer-to-Peer Events
description:
Highlights:

Location: Cyprus

Language: Fluent in Russian and English (C1+)

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About Peer-to-Peer at Fundraise Up

Peer-to-Peer turns supporters into fundraisers. Instead of only donating, a supporter creates a fundraising page, invites others to give, joins a team, or participates in an event on behalf of a nonprofit.

We are building Peer-to-Peer as a new product line. The product starts with two connected directions:

  • P2P DIY: self-serve fundraising for birthdays, memorials, personal challenges, and other supporter-led campaigns.
  • P2P Events: structured, time-bound fundraising programs such as walks, runs, rides, climbs, workplace challenges, and recurring event series.

DIY creates the product foundation. Events extends it with registration, teams and captains, event operations, participant communication, attribution, reporting, and integrations. The two directions must work as one coherent product while serving different customer workflows and levels of complexity.

About the Role

We are looking for a Product Manager to own P2P Events within the broader Peer-to-Peer product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn an ambiguous product area into a focused solution grounded in customer, usage, and commercial evidence.

Events and DIY serve different sides of the same system: nonprofits need to run fundraising programs, while participants need effective tools to fundraise. You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader P2P area so these experiences and their shared capabilities evolve together.

This is not an event-planning or project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to serve the entire category at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared P2P foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions explicit.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit event teams, participants, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow mapping, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and incumbent-product expectations.
  • Shape problems such as registration, teams and captains, attribution and reporting, event operations, participant communication, and CRM integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, and QA.
  • Ensure the product can evolve from simpler events to more advanced team structures, event series, and operational workflows without overbuilding the first release.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch and learn through EAPs with clear entry criteria, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can run events successfully and whether participants activate, fundraise, and return.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, and Support on positioning, customer commitments, enablement, and competitive context.
  • Connect product evidence to adoption, expansion, pipeline, retention, and GPV.
  • Turn evidence into clear recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with multi-actor workflows, permissions, states, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, payments, registration, events, community, or other multi-sided products.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • A strong, collaborative product team that owns what it builds
  • Clear product vision and access to real customer feedback from global nonprofit leaders
  • Flat structure: no politics, just great work with great people
  • Transparent company culture-we share how we’re growing, where revenue comes from, and what’s next
  • Long-term focus: we offer equity options and value sustained, meaningful contribution

Compensation

title: Optometrist
description:
Als optometrist bij de oogkliniek in Amsterdam heb je het voorrecht te werken in een setting die boordevol kansen zit om jezelf te ontwikkelen. We behandelen hier veel verschillende ziektebeelden die je ook in een academische setting tegen komt. Dit maakt elke dag een avontuur, waarin jij kunt groeien en bloeien!

Hoe jij impact kunt maken als Optometrist

Als Optometrist in onze oogkliniek in Amsterdam ontvang en begeleid jij de patiënten tijdens hun consulten en onderzoek. Samen met de arts draai je specialistische spreekuren zoals; retina-, orbita-, vitreoretinaal- en glaucoomspreekuur. Hier kom je situaties tegen die je elders alleen in academische omgevingen tegen zou komen. Daarnaast draai je ook zelfstandige spreekuren voor de nacontroles, met altijd een ervaren arts in huis die over je schouder meekijkt indien nodig.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Uitvoeren van gezichtsveldonderzoeken, OCT’s en biometrie

  • Administratieve taken zoals het verwerken van de patiëntinformatie en het uitwerken van consultverslagen

  • Bijwonen van het paramedici- en patiëntoverleg

  • Meedenken over de verbetering van onze processen

Wat heb je nodig om succesvol te zijn in deze rol?

  • Een HBO Optometrie diploma (of je bent nog bezig met de opleiding en behaald jouw diploma binnen een jaar)

  • Je beschikbaar bent voor 16 tot 40 uur per week, en op jouw werkdagen beschikbaar bent tussen 8:30 uur en 17:00 uur

  • Je leergierig bent en op de hoogte blijft van ontwikkelingen binnen je vakgebied.

Twijfel je of de functie als Optometrist bij Bergman Clinics bij jou past? Neem gerust contact met ons op, we denken graag met je mee!

Wat krijg je hier voor terug?

Wij geloven dat goede zorg begint bij onze medewerkers. Daarom zorgen wij goed voor jou.

Arbeidsvoorwaarden

  • Een salaris tussen €4.043,- en €6.058,- bruto per maand (FWG 55), conform cao ZKN op basis van een fulltime dienstverband (40 uur)

  • Een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,33% en vakantietoeslag van 8,33%

  • Reiskostenvergoeding van €0,23 per kilometer met een maximum van 80 km (enkele reis). Reis je met het ov? Dan vergoeden wij deze kosten volledig

  • Een contract voor bepaalde tijd met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband

  • Bij een fulltime dienstverband ontvang je 160 vakantie-uren en maar liefst 72 extra PLB-uren per kalenderjaar. Het PLB-urenbudget kent geen verjaringstermijn

  • Een toekomstbestendig pensioen bij PFZW waarbij wij beiden 50% van de pensioenpremie betalen

  • Korting op producten en/of diensten van Bey en Memira: 20% korting voor jou en 10% korting voor Friends & Family

  • Toegang tot Evermood, het welzijnsplatform waar je anoniem terechtkunt voor ondersteuning, inspiratie en coaching op het gebied van vitaliteit, werkplezier en persoonlijke groei

  • Via Alleo profiteer je van diverse fiscale voordelen, zoals een belastbaar vrij budget tot €120,- per jaar, de leasefietsregeling of een sportabonnement

  • Unlimited Learning via Good Habitz: onbeperkt toegang tot honderden trainingen en opleidingen die aansluiten op jouw wensen en ambities via onze eigen Bergman Academy

  • Mogelijkheid om deel te nemen aan een collectieve zorgverzekering bij Zilveren Kruis, Menzis of IZZ

  • En nog veel meer, zoals gratis fruit op het werk en gezellige borrels en feestjes

  • Er is een (para)medisch budget beschikbaar voor congressen

  • Vergoeding voor contributie van het OVN lidmaatschap

Daarnaast ondersteunen we je bij het op orde houden van je kwaliteitsregister en zijn er op termijn, bij goed functioneren, mogelijkheden om je verder te ontwikkelen, bijvoorbeeld richting een functie als Physician Assistant.

Waarom werken bij Bergman Clinics?
Onze collega Siraz Hadarian begon haar carrière als Optometrist bij ons en kreeg daarna de kans om door te groeien bij Bergman Clinics, waar ze nu werkt als Physician Assistant. Ze deelt graag haar ervaringen en het groeipad dat ze bij Bergman Clinics heeft doorgemaakt! Benieuwd naar haar verhaal? Klik dan hier voor het volledige interview.

Hier ga je werken
In de rol van Optometrist word je verwelkomd in onze prachtige kliniek in Amsterdam. Deze kliniek heeft een directe samenwerking met het Amsterdam UMC. Dit betekent dat je een breed spectrum aan ziektebeelden gaat tegenkomen tijdens de spreekuren.

Je komt terecht in een team diverse specialisaties. Orthoptisten, oogartsen, TOA's en mede-optometristen vormen samen een gedreven team dat streeft naar optimale zorg voor onze patiënten. En met collega's van het Amsterdam UMC die ook op de kliniek werken, is er een overvloed aan kennis en expertise om mee te sparren. Kortom, als je klaar bent voor een dynamische rol waarin je een verschil kunt maken in het leven van anderen, dan is dit dé uitdaging voor jou!

Ben je enthousiast?
Solliciteer dan via de button. Vragen? De recruiter staat voor je klaar. Stuur vrijblijvend een bericht via WhatsApp of bel gerust.
Screening van CV, diploma's, identiteitsbewijs en VOG (verklaring omtrent gedrag) zal deel uitmaken van de sollicitatieprocedure.

title: Family Coordinator WRF (77871)
description:
Wellness for Recovering Families

Job Title: Family Coordinator
Reports To: Program Director
Position Type: Full-time / Part-time

Job Summary

The Family Coordinator plays a critical role in providing comprehensive support to families impacted by substance use. Through detailed assessments, needs identification, and collaborative service coordination, the Family Coordinator ensures that families access appropriate resources across social determinants of health. This role involves direct client advocacy, service navigation, and ongoing coordination with treatment and service providers to develop and deliver effective interventions. The Family Coordinator also collaborates closely with the Peer Family Support Specialist to foster a supportive, strengths-based approach for each family, ensuring their needs are met holistically and efficiently.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Needs Assessment: Collaborate with families to identify their needs, using comprehensive assessments and screening tools to address challenges related to housing, healthcare, education, employment, substance use, and overall family stability.
  • Service Planning: Collaborate with families to develop individualized service plans based on assessment findings & the interests of the families, helping families set realistic goals and actionable steps to address identified needs.
  • Treatment Providers: Coordinate regularly with substance use treatment providers, mental health professionals, and other service agencies to facilitate integrated, family-centered support.
  • Service Coordination: Connect families with community resources, substance use treatment, recovery supports, and other essential services; facilitate referrals to external service providers when appropriate.
  • Advocacy for Families: Actively advocate for families within child welfare, treatment, legal, and social service systems, ensuring that services are accessible and responsive to their needs.
  • Data Management and Program Reporting: Maintain accurate, up-to-date records on all family interactions, assessments, and service activities, ensuring data is entered promptly into the program’s information systems.
  • Collaborative Development of New Services: Identify gaps in current resources and assist in developing new services and interventions tailored to the evolving needs of families in the program.
  • Support for Peer Family Support Specialist: Work closely with the Peer Specialist to ensure a seamless support network for families, providing guidance and assistance in service delivery.
  • Ongoing Family Communication: Establish regular check-ins with families to assess progress, adjust service plans, and respond to emerging needs.
  • Resource Development: Research and identify new services, community resources, and partnership opportunities to expand support options available to families.
  • Crisis Intervention: Provide direct support and intervention when families face immediate challenges, helping them access emergency resources and maintain stability.
  • Client Transportation: Provide transportation for clients to their initial appointments with service providers, treatment centers, or other critical resources to ensure timely access to necessary support services.

title: Voorzitter Raad van Toezicht
description:
Geef vanuit bestuurlijke senioriteit richting aan een organisatie die iedere dag werkt aan een kleurrijk leven voor mensen met een verstandelijke beperking.

Pergamijn zoekt een verbindende en toekomstgerichte voorzitter voor de Raad van Toezicht: een ervaren bestuurder of toezichthouder die zich verbonden voelt met onze cliënten, onze maatschappelijke opdracht en de professionals die daar iedere dag met passie aan werken.

Waarom Pergamijn?

Bij Pergamijn draait het om mensen. Om cliënten die zoveel mogelijk zelf de regie voeren over hun leven. Om naasten die nauw betrokken zijn. En om bevlogen professionals die samen zoeken naar wat iemand nodig heeft om zo zelfstandig en volwaardig mogelijk te leven.

Als voorzitter van de Raad van Toezicht kun je hier vanuit een betekenisvolle positie aan bijdragen. Je helpt Pergamijn haar zorg en ondersteuning duurzaam te versterken en zich voor te bereiden op de toekomst. Je houdt niet alleen toezicht, maar brengt ook perspectief, stelt de vragen die ertoe doen en draagt bij aan een organisatie die wil blijven leren, ontwikkelen en vernieuwen.

Over Pergamijn

Pergamijn ondersteunt mensen met een verstandelijke beperking in Midden-Limburg, de Westelijke Mijnstreek en Parkstad-Heuvelland. We bieden verschillende vormen van wonen, zorg, behandeling, dagbesteding en ambulante ondersteuning.

Onze cliënten voeren zoveel mogelijk zelf de regie over hun leven en nemen zo volwaardig mogelijk deel aan de samenleving. We werken vanuit de visie:

“Zo zelfstandig als mogelijk, zo beschermd als nodig.”

Samen met cliënten, hun naasten en bevlogen professionals bouwen we aan een kleurrijk leven dat past bij ieder individu. Onze vier kernwaarden geven daarbij richting: Passie voor de cliënt en ons werk, Partnerschap in de samenwerking, Professionaliteit in ons handelen en Positiviteit door te kijken naar wat wél kan. Ook van onze toezichthouders verwachten we dat zij deze waarden herkennen en uitdragen.

De Raad van Toezicht

De Raad van Toezicht bestaat uit zes leden en houdt integraal toezicht op het beleid van de Raad van Bestuur. De continuïteit en maatschappelijke doelstelling van Pergamijn staan daarbij centraal.

Het toezicht richt zich onder meer op de zorginhoudelijke en maatschappelijke opdracht, financiën en bedrijfsvoering, medezeggenschap, Governance, compliance, cultuur en maatschappelijke waardecreatie.

Daarnaast vervult de raad de werkgeversrol richting de bestuurder en fungeert hij als klankbord en adviseur. De raad werkt vanuit vertrouwen, open dialoog, kritische afstand en onafhankelijkheid.

Jouw rol als voorzitter

Als voorzitter geef je richting aan het toezichtproces en bewaak je het collegiale functioneren van de raad. Je creëert ruimte voor verschillende perspectieven en zorgt ervoor dat de deskundigheid van alle leden goed wordt benut.

Je:

  • bevordert een open, professionele en constructieve samenwerking;

  • bewaakt de kwaliteit en effectiviteit van het toezicht;

  • fungeert als stevig en vertrouwd klankbord voor de bestuurder;

  • geeft samen met de raad invulling aan de werkgeversrol;

  • stimuleert reflectie en verdere professionalisering;

  • stimuleert vernieuwing en stelt toekomstgerichte vragen;

  • ziet toe op de naleving van geldende Governance principes;

  • vertegenwoordigt de Raad van Toezicht richting externe belanghebbenden;

  • helpt de raad en bestuurder relevante maatschappelijke en zorginhoudelijke ontwikkelingen tijdig te herkennen.

Wie zoeken wij?

We zoeken een senior, verbindend en integer voorzitter met een stevig bestuurlijk profiel. Je onderschrijft de missie, visie en kernwaarden van Pergamijn en voelt je oprecht betrokken bij onze cliënten, hun naasten en onze maatschappelijke opdracht. Met jouw achtergrond en persoonlijkheid ben je een waardevolle aanvulling op de raad.

Je:

  • hebt ruime bestuurlijke en/of toezichthoudende ervaring;

  • hebt bij voorkeur ervaring als lid of voorzitter van een Raad van Toezicht;

  • hebt affiniteit met de gehandicaptenzorg en de leefwereld van cliënten;

  • onderschrijft het belang van inspraak en medezeggenschap en stimuleert dit actief;

  • hebt oog voor kwaliteit van bestaan, kwaliteit van zorg en een veilige woon- en leefomgeving;

  • bent in staat langdurige strategische ontwikkelingen te overzien en te beoordelen, zonder de dagelijkse praktijk van cliënten uit het oog te verliezen;

  • beschikt over natuurlijk gezag en bestuurlijke senioriteit;

  • brengt mensen, belangen en verschillende perspectieven samen;

  • bewaart rust en overzicht bij complexe vraagstukken;

  • beschikt over onafhankelijk oordeelsvermogen;

  • stelt kritische vragen en durft zo nodig een afwijkend standpunt in te nemen;

  • handelt integer, transparant en vanuit sterke ethische normen;

  • bent organisatiesensitief, reflectief en samenwerkingsgericht;

  • beschikt over een relevant maatschappelijk en bestuurlijk netwerk;

  • hebt voldoende tijd en beschikbaarheid om het voorzitterschap effectief te vervullen.

Onafhankelijkheid en bezoldiging

Als voorzitter heb je geen belangen die strijdig zijn met de functie of met Pergamijn. Je handelt volgens de Governance code Zorg, de statuten, reglementen, toezichtvisie en kernwaarden van de organisatie.

De bezoldiging is vastgesteld binnen de kaders van de Wet normering topinkomens en de richtlijnen van de NVTZ. Reis- en onkosten worden volgens de geldende regeling vergoed.

Interesse en procedure

Wil jij vanuit jouw ervaring en maatschappelijke betrokkenheid bijdragen aan de toekomst van Pergamijn? Stuur dan je motivatiebrief en curriculum vitae uiterlijk donderdag 17 september om 12.00 uur naar raadvantoezicht@pergamijn.org.

De briefselectie is op woensdag 23 september en de selectiegesprekken worden gehouden op vrijdag 16 oktober tussen 13.00-18.00 uur in Sittard. De voorkeurskandidaten worden vervolgens uitgenodigd voor een tweede gesprek met de adviescommissie op donderdagmiddag 22 oktober tussen 15.00-17.00 uur, eveneens in Sittard.

We vragen kandidaten om bij hun sollicitatie alvast rekening te houden met deze data.

Voor meer informatie is Hans Hendrikx, voorzitter van de Raad van Toezicht, bereikbaar op 8, 10 en 15 september van 17.00-19.00 uur. Voor het maken van een afspraak kun je contact opnemen met het bestuurssecretariaat via raadvantoezicht@pergamijn.org.

title: Founding Engineer, Robot Behavior and Decision-Making
description:
The Bigger Picture

At Andromeda, we're building the social intelligence layer for humanoid robots - technology that allows robots to understand people, build relationships and become a meaningful part of everyday life.

Our first robot, Abi, is already doing this in aged care and healthcare, where she brings conversation, companionship and engagement to people every day.

Now we're scaling from early deployments into a platform that can operate across thousands of real-world environments. We're looking for individuals who want to tackle hard problems across robotics and AI, and help define what it means for robots to live and interact alongside people.

The Role

We are looking for an engineer to found our Mission Autonomy team, which will own our robot’s long-duration decision-making layer and orchestrate the totality of Abi’s day. Mission Autonomy continuously decides what Abi should do next, balances task-level trade-offs, and adapts the robot’s plan across an eight-hour shift. It sits above and orchestrates Abi’s existing layers that perform conversations, waypoint navigation and obstacle avoidance, perception, gestures, and operator tooling.

As the founding Mission Autonomy team member, you will propose and build Andromeda’s Mission Autonomy (MA) architecture from the ground up, using frontier models and evaluation (both sim and real-world) to train and launch MA, and work with our voice agent, mobile autonomy, and gestures teams to design harnesses through which MA can execute behaviors on Abi. Once built, MA should guide Abi through a home, choose when to join an interaction, keep her character, and recover when the plan breaks. There is no playbook for this. You’ll need a keen eye for model evaluation and trade-offs, balancing architectural leadership with strategic hands-on work. The work combines research with practical robotics.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design the system. Challenge our initial concepts as you discover what a full shift actually needs: is it formulated as an agent harness ingesting scene graphs and acting over robust, typed action primitives? Or will you invoke World Models and VLA components? You will shape the Mission Autonomy roadmap for Andromeda.
  • Prototype the system. Get a mission autonomy loop running in simulation early. Use it to decide what we build, before the company commits teams to an architecture.
  • Co-design and build simulation capabilities with our simulation engineer.
  • Own the technical direction and run the design conversations with autonomy, chatbot, perception, audio and platform teams. Turn them into contracts those teams can build against.
  • Shape the action primitives. Work out what the mission needs from the layers underneath. Specify it properly. Get it built, whether that means convincing the owning team or writing it yourself.
  • Design for degradation. Define how Abi should behave when audio, perception, connectivity, navigation, or platform health degrades. Make those moments safe, useful, and legible to operators, while preserving Abi’s character rather than treating every failure as a generic error state.
  • Establish deployment patterns. Create a repeatable path from simulation prototypes to demonstrations on the robot, with the configuration, observability, test gates, and rollback mechanisms needed to iterate safely.
  • Build the evaluation system. Define benchmarking protocols, evaluation methods, and reporting that let us continuously measure the longest-horizon missions Abi can complete, the interventions they require, and the failure modes that limit them.

Your first 90 days

Month 1: Learn about Abi in the real world: read the Concept of Operations document, challenge its assumptions, and spend time with Abi in an aged-care home. Bring the autonomy, conversational AI, perception, audio, platform, and simulation teams together to define how the system makes decisions and how the layers work together. Deliver the first architecture and a clear six-month build plan, including what not to build.

Month 2: Build a working slice in simulation: Abi drives to a resident’s room, arrives safely, and starts a conversation. Use simulation to discover what breaks when the resident is absent, the route changes, or a subsystem degrades. Turn those lessons into better interfaces, a repeatable evaluation harness, and the next set of hypotheses and assumptions to test.

Month 3: Take the prototype from simulation to Abi in the lab. Establish the deployment, monitoring, replay, and evaluation patterns that show how far Abi can run autonomously, what stops her, and why.

Requirements

Skills and Experience Required

  • 5+ years of experience building autonomous systems, with an MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Previous autonomy experience in areas such as self-driving, mobile robotics, warehouse robotics, field robotics, or similar, including at least one deployment lifecycle from concept through deployment and operations.
  • Experience with ROS 2, Nav2, and simulation tools such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or MuJoCo.
  • Awareness of safety-critical design principles for robots operating around people.
  • Strong software engineering skills in Python, C++, or Rust. Comfortable working across the stack, from high-level planning and behavior to low-level robot interfaces and runtime constraints.
  • Practical robotics experience. Comfortable bringing up hardware, debugging sensors and actuators, and tinkering with the robot in the office.
  • Strong communication and influence skills, particularly when working across Australian teams and with engineers whose systems you do not directly own.
  • Architecture and software depth. Able to steer the system design, define interfaces and contracts, and write the first versions of the primitives rather than wait for another team.

Bonus points

  • Experience building mission autonomy systems in robotics, defense technology, or similar domains.
  • Research experience, ideally at master’s or PhD level, applying LLM techniques to long-duration robotic task planning, orchestration, tool use, or error recovery.
  • Experience designing simulation-based evaluation systems, including benchmarks, scenario harnesses, metrics, failure taxonomies, and reporting for long-horizon missions.
  • Experience with robot planning and behavior architectures, including Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), task-and-motion planning, behavior trees, or finite-state machines for baselining.
  • Technical judgment. Able to reason about trade-offs explicitly, and earn the trust of senior autonomy engineers and the teams that own adjacent parts of the stack.

Benefits

The expected base salary for this role is $200,000 to $240,000 USD. Actual compensation will be determined by a variety of factors, including the candidates’ job related knowledge, skills and experience.

If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, that’s okay; we still encourage you to apply. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Our Values

  • Empathy – Kindness and compassion are at the heart of everything we do.
  • Play – Play sharpens focus. It keeps us curious, fast and obsessed with the craft.
  • Never Settle – A relentless ambition, bias toward action, and uncomfortable levels of curiosity.
  • Tenacity – Tenacious under pressure, we assume chaos and stay in motion to adapt and progress.
  • Unity – Different minds. Shared mission. No passengers.

Let’s build the future together.

SUMMARY OF KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position is responsible for the day-to-day management of all aspects of the restaurant. In doing so, the AGM will exercise the appropriate level of discipline and supervision to ensure that team members work within the budgetary and cost controlling objectives that are established by our corporate offices. The AGM is also the designee from management who is assigned to take steps to direct the staff in a way to ensure that all sanitation, safety and food quality obligations are met or exceeded on a consistent basis.

  • Manage, supervise and direct all hourly employees including with respect to their daily activities, work assignments, time off requests and unique needs.

  • Follow Operations Playbook to ensure consistent daily operations (and take appropriate actions when staff members fail to comply).
  • Utilize digital manager logbook to communicate shift notes, product needs, equipment repairs, and staffing notes with management team.
  • Enforcing appropriate security measures at the restaurant so that the safety of our employees and guests are always maintained (this may include counseling, re-training or discipline when deemed appropriate by the AGM).
  • Manage and make recommendations to help control the costs of food, supplies, and liquor expenses including conducting weekly inventory and recommending adjustments when necessary.
  • Understanding, managing, and practicing safe food handling procedures and enforcing those procedures for all other staff members.
  • Adhere to company policies, procedures, all state and federal wage and hour regulations, and restaurant filing responsibilities.
  • Ensure all equipment is in good repair and/or taking steps to ensure repairs are made and/or equipment is taken out of duty to avoid injury or accident to others if deemed appropriate in the discretion of the AGM.
  • Manage all processes including line checks, pull thaw, prep lists, food inventory, beverage cost, truck orders, food safety, etc.

  • Responsible for execution of new initiatives including new product and menu rollouts; this aspect of the job requires creativity and initiatives of the individual AGM.

title: Senior Technical Project Manager
description:
About the job

Own the plan that turns complex test strategy into manufacturing readiness for new Graphcore products.

As Senior Project Manager within Product Test and Diagnosis, you will plan and coordinate manufacturing test delivery for New Product Introductions. You will connect activity across Chip Test, Board Test, System Test, Lab and Silicon Characterisation teams.

Your work will help Graphcore move from product roadmap to manufacturing readiness with clarity and control. You will align engineering, operations and external partners around scope, milestones, risks and decisions.

You will build end-to-end plans, manage dependencies and keep technical programmes moving across regions. You will also coordinate DfX reviews and improve how test, lab and characterisation work is planned.

This role sits where hardware, manufacturing and execution meet. You will help teams see what is coming and act before risks become blockers.

The Team and culture

The Product Test and Diagnosis team identifies and diagnoses hardware defects across silicon, boards, server blades and rack-scale systems. The team owns test strategy across manufacturing and deployed field environments.

Work happens across global teams in the UK, Taiwan, India and the United States. You will bring structure, pace and ownership to work spanning engineering, operations and manufacturing partners.

Decisions are made through clear plans, visible risks and practical trade-offs. You will help teams speak up early, align fast and take responsibility for delivery.

What we’re looking for

· Strong programme and project management skills across hardware-centric, cross-functional programmes.
· Ability to tailor delivery methods, including waterfall, Agile or Scrum, to fit technical delivery.
· Experience driving alignment across engineering, operations and geographically distributed teams.
· Confidence managing complex dependencies across technical teams, suppliers and manufacturing constraints.
· Working knowledge of tools such as JIRA, Confluence, MS Project or equivalent.
· Experience in semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, manufacturing test, lab or silicon characterisation programmes.

While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences. We also welcome engineers returning to the profession after a career break, including through returnship routes.

Benefits

· Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
· Comprehensive healthcare cover: Medical insurance for you and your eligible family members, alongside outpatient care and mental health support
· Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
· Financial protection: Life and personal accident insurance to help provide peace of mind for you and your loved ones
· Monthly wellbeing allowance: A cash allowance to support your everyday wellbeing, whether that's meals, fitness, travel, broadband or other lifestyle expenses
· Additional family and lifestyle support: Including relocation assistance, childcare reimbursement, annual health check-ups, referral bonuses and a marriage gift, where eligible
· Enhanced family leave: Comprehensive maternity, paternity and adoption leave, helping you balance your career with family life
· Learning and development opportunities: Access to training and development resources to help you grow your skills and career
· Inclusive workplace: A collaborative, diverse environment with initiatives that support inclusion, wellbeing and employee development

We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.
We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.

Sponsorship

Applicants must have the legal right to work in India. Unfortunately, we are unable to provide visa sponsorship or support visa applications for this role.

Join the Team at Graphcore

Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.

As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.

Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore brings together deep expertise to solve complex problems and deliver meaningful progress in AI compute.

If you want to bring structure, pace and clarity to complex manufacturing test programmes, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now to be part of the journey.

description:
Head of Investment Advisory

Location: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

Workplace Type: On-site


About the Role

Are you passionate about transforming macro research, investment strategies, and market data into tangible value for clients? Do you envision building a standardized "One House View" that empowers hundreds of Relationship Managers (RMs) and Advisors to offer unified investment advice? If you're driven to elevate Wealth Management in Vietnam to global standards, where every recommendation is personalized to client goals and risk appetites, this unique opportunity at ACB might be for you. ACB is embarking on a significant transformation to establish a next-generation Wealth Management model, moving beyond mere financial product offerings to become a long-term partner in wealth planning, management, and growth. This role is not a traditional portfolio management position; you will be a core member in designing the investment advisory platforms for ACB's Wealth Management division. The frameworks, model portfolios, risk assessment tools, and investment perspectives you develop will be instrumental for our expert advisors across the entire network, serving our valued Wealth clients.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain a unified "One House View" by synthesizing insights from Research, Fund Management, and market data, translating them into consistent investment perspectives for various market scenarios and guiding asset allocation principles.
  • Design and implement a robust Model Portfolio system, creating standardized portfolios tailored to different risk tolerance levels, establishing principles for asset allocation, rebalancing, and risk management, ensuring alignment with diverse Wealth client segments.
  • Develop comprehensive Risk Profiling frameworks and Goal-based Investing tools, including designing assessment instruments for risk appetite, linking risk profiles to asset allocation and model portfolios, and creating tools to help clients define long-term financial objectives.
  • Build and manage a data library and advisory tools, standardizing key macro, market, and risk indicators, collaborating with Data & Technology teams to develop dashboards and data repositories, and transforming in-depth research into easily digestible content for RMs and clients.
  • Monitor portfolio performance and conduct stress testing, regularly evaluating portfolio effectiveness, developing market scenarios for stress testing, and providing recommendations for adjustments aligned with investment objectives and risk appetites.


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Over 15 years of experience in investment, research, or portfolio management within asset management firms, securities companies, or banks.
  • Deep understanding of macroeconomics, financial markets, and portfolio theory.
  • Proven ability to translate academic research and market analysis into practical advisory solutions.
  • Experience in building Asset Allocation strategies or Model Portfolios is a significant advantage.
  • Possess a long-term, objective, and client-centric mindset.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of conveying technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in financial modeling and data analysis tools.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Economics, or a related quantitative field.


Additional Information

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the strategic direction and foundational architecture of Wealth Management at ACB. You will be instrumental in building a standardized investment advisory system for the entire Wealth Management division, defining the investment philosophy and asset management principles for Wealth clients, and enhancing the capability of RMs to transition from product sales to solution-based advisory. You will contribute to creating one of the most modern and differentiated Wealth Management platforms in the market. This is an ideal position for individuals seeking to make a strategic impact at the model and platform level, rather than solely managing individual investment portfolios. If you are an investment expert, investment strategist, or portfolio manager looking to co-create the future of Wealth Management in Vietnam with ACB, we encourage you to apply or refer suitable candidates to lettm03@acb.com.vn. We look forward to connecting with talented professionals who share our vision.

title: Storage Operations Engineer
description:
Qube Research & Technologies (QRT) is a global quantitative and systematic investment manager, operating in all liquid asset classes across the world. Your Future Role Within QRT

The team is looking for a Storage Operations Engineer to join a newly established local team in Hong Kong, working closely alongside our current team in London.

The successful candidate will work directly with our research and trading teams, focusing on the scalable storage component of our high-performance computing (HPC) on-premises environment. Ideally, you will have a technical background in supporting, operating, and maintaining Linux-based, large-scale, high-performance workloads. Experience with S3, NFS, NVMEoF, and RoCE, as well as vendors such as VAST, WEKA, NetApp, or DDN, would be highly advantageous.

In addition to supporting our user base (many based in APAC), you will liaise directly with vendors to manage the deployment, upgrade, and maintenance of storage infrastructure, and play a key role in incident management, responding calmly and effectively under pressure.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong enterprise storage administration experience who is looking to grow into a modern, high-performance, petabyte-scale storage environment.

Your Present Skillsets

  • 4+ years of experience in storage systems administration and hands-on experience managing large-scale storage environments (petabyte scale preferred), ideally within an HPC or research-driven environment
  • A solid understanding of storage protocols across POSIX-compliant filesystems and S3
  • Knowledge of storage benchmarking, analysis, tuning, and optimization across Linux kernel tuning, network, and storage performance
  • Working knowledge of DevOps tooling, including Terraform, Ansible, Vault, GitLab, and Temporal
  • Working knowledge of Python and/or Golang
  • Strong knowledge of infrastructure metric visualization using Prometheus or Victoria Logs and Grafana
  • Preferably, expertise with container technologies such as Docker and orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes

Do you envision yourself working for a dynamic, mission-driven organization which supports the community while fostering an employee culture of appreciation and fun? If your answer is yes, then an employment opportunity at Directions for Living may be a great fit for you!

POSITION SUMMARY:

This is a professional position providing peer recovery support in the Together We Rise program under the Families First Division. The Families First Division was created as a result of the Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA) which is focused on keeping children safely with their families to avoid the trauma that results when children are placed in out-of-home care. The Families First Division operates with the understanding that children do best in a strong family, and that children and their families do best with the support of their communities. To increase the number of children who can remain safely at home with their families, the law provided families with greater access to mental health services, substance use treatment, and/or improved parenting skills. The Families First Division ensures that families have time sensitive access to mental health, substance use treatment and supportive services focused on strengthening families and proactively supports those children at risk of child abuse, neglect and separation from their family. All Families First programming works together, alongside the parent/ caregiver to decrease the number of children entering the Child Welfare System by utilizing a solution-focused, family centered approach and evidenced based or research supported practices to assist families in meeting needs and goals while preventing further incidents of child abuse, neglect and abandonment. Staff in Together We Rise will work specifically with the parents/caregivers and the children who have come to the attention of the child protective investigation division of the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office, and who have been determined to be safe but at high or very high risk of future child abuse, and neglect. Together We Rise (TWR) will work with all members of the family with a team-based approach in a supportive, empowering and respectful manner to assist the family with creating safe and stable parenting practices to facilitate long-term behavior change that will ensure that children are safe in their home.

The Together We Rise (TWR) Peer Mentor will play an integral role of support, coaching and guidance for families at risk of becoming involved in the child welfare system in Pinellas County. The TWR Peer Mentor is assigned to work with parents with a substance abuse, mental health or co-occurring mental health & substance abuse concern and is responsible for guiding the family and serving as a system navigator who supports the parent in treatment/recovery. The TWR Peer Mentor will ensure that the peer services being delivered are individualized, recovery-focused and allow individuals the opportunity to learn how to manage their own recovery and advocacy process. The TWR Peer Mentor will be a subject matter expert through lived experience and will serve to enhance the development of natural supports, as well as coping and self-management skills. The TWR Peer Mentor will ensure that peer services emphasize personal safety, self-worth, confidence, and growth, connection to the community, boundary setting, planning, self-advocacy, personal fulfillment, and development of social supports, and effective communication. The TWR Peer Mentor focus services on emphasizing the acquisition; development; and expansion of rehabilitative skills needed to move forward in recovery. The TWR Peer will ensure collaboration with the other clinical service providers, such as the Behavioral Health Case Manager, therapist and/or a psychiatrist. If the parent/s are not engaged in these clinical services, the TWR Peer Mentor will notify the program supervisor/director and help provide education on these services and help to coordinate initiation, as clinically appropriate. If these services are recommended, but parent/s are not yet willing to engage, this should be documented in the service notes and the TWR Peer Mentor will be responsible for completing the documentation. This is a field position. The Peer Mentor is responsible for ensuring an annual client facing client care number of 1,410 hours annually. Achieving the minimum required weekly, monthly and annual client facing client care hours is an essential function of this positon.

Directions for Living is an essential services provider. All Directions for Living Team Members must be willing and able to provide vital support and essential services to the people that we serve in the event of an emergency, pandemic or other disaster situation.

With 18 retail stores, an online store, an extensive reuse/recycling operation, and our Contract Services division, we help individuals overcome barriers to employment, build sustainable lives and communities.

The Retail Donor Greeter I is responsible for providing exceptional customer service by welcoming donors, accepting donations, and ensuring a positive donation experience. This role supports efficient store operations by receiving, separating, and preparing donated goods for processing, maintaining a clean and organized donation area, and following all safety and operational procedures.   • Ensure all boxes have proper labeling.

  • Properly loads and prepares trucks for pick up by transportation.

  • Follows and enforces all company procedures.

  • Stays up to date on all safety and equipment certifications as needed.

  • Performs other duties as requested.

Responsibilities may be added, deleted or changed at any time at the management's discretion, formally or informally either orally or in writing.

Key Performance Indicator

  • Sort 1 bin of collected raw donations every 15–20 minutes consistently during shift.

location: Corporate Rancho Cucamonga - Rancho Cucamonga, CA 91730

title: EVS Tech I (Full-time, 2:00pm-10:30pm, with rotating weekends)

description:
Organization Overview, Mission, Vision, and Values

Our mission is to improve the health of people in the communities we serve through compassionate, high-quality care, prevention, and wellness education.
